chunks: My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Sa’d bin Abdullah, from Ahmad bin Muhammad, from his father, from Muhammad bin Yahya, from Hammad bin Uthman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said to a man: O such-a-person, what is it with you and your brother?
He said: May I be sacrificed for you, there was something to me upon him (to fulfil), so I inquired about my right.

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) then said: Inform me about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: «and they fear a bad (result from the) reckoning». Do you see that they feared that He will tyrannize against them or wrong them? No, however, they feared inquiry and detailing (in questioning).
ai.seo_question: What does 'bad reckoning' mean in Shia interpretation?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the fear of 'bad reckoning' (su' al-hisab) stems not from divine injustice, but from the believer's anxiety over excessive scrutiny (istiqsa) and minute detailing of deeds. This interpretation, rooted in the chain of transmission through Shaykh al-Saduq, underscores a key Shia theological nuance where human accountability is viewed with profound humility, emphasizing that the severity of judgment lies in the precision of divine observation rather than any potential bias.

He said: May I be sacrificed for you, there was something to me upon him (to fulfil), so I inquired about my right.

Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, then said: Inform me about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: «and they fear a bad (result from the) reckoning» [13:21]. Do you see that they feared that He will tyrannize against them or wrong them? No, however, they feared inquiry and detailing (in questioning).
